sourceObjectiveEnglish: Tell what happened yesterday: The preterite reports completed past actions.
sourceSpeakingEnglish: Role-play Una tarde diferente with a patient classmate. Practice tell what happened yesterday. Use this lesson's grammar, ask a related question, answer the partner, and confirm understanding. Keep language at beginner level; explain unfamiliar words in English when asked.

sourceGrammarEnglish.focus: The preterite reports completed past actions. Regular -ar endings include -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -aron; -er/-ir include -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -ieron. Written accents matter.

examples.es: Terminamos la tarea a las cinco.
examples.en: We finished the homework at five.

cards.decisionNote: French le must be attached to a masculine noun and may elide; source el is a masculine singular article.
Spanish la groups feminine article, it and her; French la/l’ as article or object cannot be one context-free scored face.
Spanish un and French un align only with masculine nouns; contextual noun agreement remains required.
Source en groups in/on/at; French dans, sur, à or au depends on the phrase.
Spanish las groups feminine plural article and object them; French les is gender-neutral and role-dependent.
Professora marks a female teacher; French enseignante preserves gender, while professeure may be preferred by locale/register.
Spanish preterite estudié uses a simple completed past; proposed French passé composé requires a curriculum decision.

cards.sourceSpanish: Terminamos la tarea a las cinco.
cards.sourceEnglish: We finished the homework at five.
cards.proposedFrench: Nous avons terminé les devoirs à cinq heures.
cards.decisionNote: Source tarea is singular homework/task; les devoirs is natural homework usage but changes grammatical number.

cards.sourceSpanish: Diego compró pan en la tienda.
cards.sourceEnglish: Diego bought bread at the store.
cards.proposedFrench: Diego a acheté du pain au magasin.
cards.decisionNote: Source en la tienda means at the store; au magasin is conditional for location and store sense.

cards.proposedFrench: Nous avons mangé dans le parc.
cards.decisionNote: Source en el parque is in the park; dans le parc keeps interior sense, but au parc may be idiomatic by context.

cards.sourceSpanish: Julia escribió un mensaje a su hermana.
cards.sourceEnglish: Julia wrote a message to her sister.
cards.proposedFrench: Julia a écrit un message à sa sœur.
cards.decisionNote: French sa agrees with sœur; source su does not mark the possessed noun’s gender.

cards.proposedFrench: Ensuite, nous sommes rentrés à pied.
cards.decisionNote: Rentrer à pied preserves walking home but could imply return rather than simply walking toward home; qualify before selection.

cards.sourceEnglish: Yesterday I studied in the library.
cards.proposedFrench: Hier, j’ai étudié à la bibliothèque.
cards.decisionNote: French à la bibliothèque uses a locative preposition where source uses en; assess exact sense in context.

reader.decisionNote: Source preterite versus French passé composé needs a curriculum decision; no answer is selected.

reader.sourceSpanish: Terminamos la tarea a las cinco.
reader.sourceEnglish: We finished the homework at five.
reader.proposedFrench: Nous avons terminé les devoirs à cinq heures.
reader.decisionNote: Source singular tarea versus proposed plural devoirs needs meaning and saved-card review.

reader.sourceSpanish: Diego compró pan en la tienda.
reader.sourceEnglish: Diego bought bread at the store.
reader.proposedFrench: Diego a acheté du pain au magasin.
reader.decisionNote: At the store is proposed au magasin, retaining the store rather than a new destination.

reader.proposedFrench: Nous avons mangé dans le parc.
reader.decisionNote: Source in the park is proposed dans le parc; au parc is a contextual alternative.

reader.sourceSpanish: Julia escribió un mensaje a su hermana.
reader.sourceEnglish: Julia wrote a message to her sister.
reader.proposedFrench: Julia a écrit un message à sa sœur.
reader.decisionNote: Sa agrees with sœur in French; source su is not gender-marked.

reader.proposedFrench: Ensuite, nous sommes rentrés à pied.
reader.decisionNote: Rentrer à pied retains walking home but adds return nuance; qualified choice required.

reader.sourceEnglish: Yesterday I studied in the library.
reader.proposedFrench: Hier, j’ai étudié à la bibliothèque.
Nous avons mangé à la cafétéria.
reader.decisionNote: Source cafetería is cafeteria, not a café; cafétéria is a conditional locale choice.

reader.sourceSpanish: Mis amigos hablaron con la profesora.
reader.sourceEnglish: My friends spoke with the teacher.
reader.proposedFrench: Mes amis ont parlé avec l’enseignante.
reader.decisionNote: Source profesora is female teacher; enseignante preserves gender; professeure is a contextual alternative.

reader.sourceEnglish: Did you finish the homework yesterday?
reader.decisionNote: Source informal singular terminaste is proposed as informal singular as-tu; register needs review.

archivedRedesign.title: Raconter une sortie passée dans l’ordre
archivedRedesign.scene: Une visite au musée a changé à cause de la pluie. Un ami demande quel événement est arrivé d’abord et pourquoi le groupe a modifié son trajet.
archivedRedesign.reason: The archived rainy museum outing changes the source yesterday-at-school events, characters and completed-past objective; it cannot inherit this lesson's saved positions or recordings.

sourceDecisions: The source objective teaches Spanish preterite for completed past actions; French passé composé is proposed only conditionally. Qualified curriculum review must decide the adaptation and Master-stage placement.
Source tarea is singular while natural French homework often uses plural les devoirs; choose a contextual phrase and dictionary/saved-item mapping.
Source la, las and en group senses that cannot map to a single context-free French scored answer; show articles, object pronouns, gender and locatives directly in final teaching.
Source profesora is a female teacher; qualify enseignante versus professeure by locale/register and preserve the female reference.
Source walk home, cafeteria, store, park and informal singular final question need exact meaning and register review before selecting French.
